description: Count matching jobs without listing them. This is the live count; prefer it over market_lookup and market_breakdown for "how many" and "which employers are hiring". A count by title_advanced with no company, company_id or job_id is an estimate (count_is_estimate is true); if it is refused as too slow, add one of those three filters or count by title. Counting by q also needs a title or company filter. Counting by description alone returns an estimate: count_is_estimate is true and count_margin gives the 95% range. To answer "which companies are hiring for X" or "how are these jobs split by ...", pass group_by: employer (company works too), work_arrangement (remote, hybrid or in_person), title, state (US), city, country or employment_type. The answer then also has group_by, groups (the top 25 values by number of matching jobs, each with value and jobs), groups_from_jobs (how many matching jobs the breakdown is based on), groups_sampled (true when this is not an exact count of every match) and groups_unknown_jobs (jobs with no known value). The breakdown is exact up to 3,000 matching jobs, estimate from a random sample above. Either way the top 25 values are returned. Above 3,000, groups_are_estimates is true, groups_note states the sample size in plain words, and each jobs number is scaled from that random sample of matching jobs (picked by job id, which is random) up to the total, not a raw sample count. If the breakdown times out, the count is still returned with no groups and groups_note says the breakdown timed out. A job with several locations or postings can count under more than one value. group_by employer keeps its own keys: employers (each with employer_name, company_id and jobs), employers_from_jobs, employers_sampled and employers_unknown_jobs, and when the breakdown is an estimate, employers_are_estimates and employers_note. When a filter is too broad to count exactly in time, count is an estimate: the answer then has count_is_estimate: true, count_margin (the 95% range either side of count) and count_note.

country.description: One or more two-letter country codes, comma-separated or as an array (US,CA).

description_advanced.description: Boolean search of the job description. AND, OR, NOT, brackets and "quoted phrases", with an operator between every two words or groups: write nurse AND NOT manager (never nurse NOT manager), and keep at least one word that is not negated. At most 200 characters and 64 words or operators. Example: python AND (sql OR "data analysis") AND NOT intern.

employment_type.description: One or more employment type values, comma-separated or as an array.

first_seen_since.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO time; jobs we first found on or after it. For a daily check for new jobs, pass the time of the last check.

near.description: A US place to search around: a ZIP code (78701), a city with its state (Austin, TX), or latitude,longitude. Use with radius_miles.

pay_min.description: Lowest yearly pay, in pay_currency (default USD). Hourly pay is about yearly / 2,080, so $45 an hour is about 93,600.

posted_since.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO time; jobs posted on or after it.

q.description: Words matched against title and description, ranked by relevance. Every word must match; for a list of skills where any may match, use description_advanced with OR, for example python OR sql OR "data analysis".

remote.description: true is the same as work_arrangement=remote.

state.description: US state, two letters (CA) or full name.

title.description: One phrase in the job title, words in order. For words in any order or Boolean logic use title_advanced.

title_advanced.description: Boolean search of the job title, words in any order. AND, OR, NOT, brackets and "quoted phrases", with an operator between every two words or groups: write nurse AND NOT manager (never nurse NOT manager), and keep at least one word that is not negated. At most 200 characters and 64 words or operators. Example: (engineer OR developer) AND NOT manager. For one phrase in order use title.

work_arrangement.description: remote, hybrid or in_person; comma-separate several.

group_by.description: Break the matching jobs down by employer (company), work_arrangement, title, state, city, country or employment_type.

name: count_jobs
title: Count jobs
